lead_cast: Marlon Brando, Al Pacino, James Caan
blurb: Puzo co-wrote the screenplay with Coppola, which is partly why the film captures the novel's weight so completely. Decades later it remains the benchmark for the crime epic.

lead_cast: Tim Robbins, Morgan Freeman, Bob Gunton
blurb: Adapted from a novella in King's collection Different Seasons. A box-office disappointment on release, it became a cultural fixture through home video and television.

lead_cast: Gregory Peck, Mary Badham, Phillip Alford
blurb: Harper Lee saw her Pulitzer-winning novel brought to screen with unusual restraint. Gregory Peck's Atticus Finch became definitive and, for Lee, essentially the final word on the character.

lead_cast: Sam Neill, Laura Dern, Jeff Goldblum
blurb: Spielberg kept Crichton's premise but softened the novel's darker edges. The result reinvented the summer blockbuster and introduced CG dinosaurs that still hold up.

lead_cast: Jack Nicholson, Shelley Duvall, Danny Lloyd
blurb: Kubrick's cold, geometric vision diverged sharply from King's novel. King disliked it enough to produce his own miniseries years later; audiences and critics ended up on Kubrick's side.

movie_title: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest
lead_cast: Jack Nicholson, Brad Dourif, Louise Fletcher
book_title: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest
blurb: Forman dropped Chief's voice-over narration from Kesey's novel, shifting the centre of gravity to McMurphy. It swept the five major Oscars — only the third film ever to do so.

lead_cast: Edward Norton, Brad Pitt, Helena Bonham Carter
blurb: Fincher kept Palahniuk's premise and much of his dialogue, altering only the ending. The novelist has said the film improved on his book.

lead_cast: Malcolm McDowell, Patrick Magee, Carl Duering
blurb: Kubrick worked from the American edition of Burgess's novel, which omitted the final chapter and its moral turn. Burgess spent the rest of his life explaining the difference.

lead_cast: Javier Bardem, Tommy Lee Jones, Josh Brolin
blurb: The Coen brothers followed McCarthy's novel almost line for line, preserving its silences and its refusal to romanticize violence.

lead_cast: Ben Affleck, Rosamund Pike, Neil Patrick Harris
blurb: Flynn adapted her own novel, trimming the plot but keeping its central cruelty intact. Fincher's cold palette matched the material exactly.

lead_cast: Jodie Foster, Anthony Hopkins, Scott Glenn
blurb: Demme turned Harris's procedural thriller into something closer to a chamber piece. Hopkins's Lecter appears for roughly sixteen minutes and dominates the film.

movie_title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
lead_cast: Daniel Craig, Rooney Mara, Christopher Plummer
book_title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
blurb: Fincher's second pass at the material after the Swedish version. Rooney Mara took her Lisbeth to a quieter, more wounded register than Noomi Rapace's.

movie_title: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring
lead_cast: Elijah Wood, Ian McKellen, Viggo Mortensen
blurb: Jackson condensed Tolkien's opening volume without losing the novel's weight. The three-film project became one of cinema's most faithful large-scale adaptations.

movie_title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
lead_cast: Daniel Radcliffe, Rupert Grint, Emma Watson
book_title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
blurb: Columbus's faithful first chapter set the visual template that seven more films would build on. Even small details, down to Hogwarts' banners, matched Rowling's descriptions.

lead_cast: Jennifer Lawrence, Josh Hutcherson, Liam Hemsworth
blurb: Collins helped adapt her own novel. Lawrence's Katniss carried the franchise and recalibrated what a YA lead could look like on screen.

lead_cast: Timothée Chalamet, Rebecca Ferguson, Oscar Isaac
blurb: Villeneuve took only the first half of Herbert's dense novel, giving each sequence room to breathe. Earlier adaptations had failed by trying to compress too much.

lead_cast: Harrison Ford, Rutger Hauer, Sean Young
book_title: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
blurb: Scott kept the question — what is a human? — and discarded most of Dick's plot. The novel's electric sheep and Mercerism never made it to screen; the film invented its own iconography.

lead_cast: Suraj Sharma, Irrfan Khan, Ayush Tandon
blurb: Ang Lee turned a novel long considered unfilmable into one of the first films where CG water looked right. The frame story keeps Martel's central ambiguity intact.

lead_cast: James McAvoy, Keira Knightley, Saoirse Ronan
blurb: Joe Wright's long tracking shot through Dunkirk became the film's signature. The ending still works because McEwan's structure survives the move to screen.

lead_cast: Ralph Fiennes, Juliette Binoche, Willem Dafoe
blurb: Minghella reshaped Ondaatje's fragmentary novel into something more linear. Ondaatje worked on the adaptation and signed off on the changes.

lead_cast: Timothée Chalamet, Armie Hammer, Michael Stuhlbarg
blurb: Guadagnino kept Aciman's languorous Italian summer and condensed the ending. Chalamet's final-shot performance became the film's most-discussed moment.

lead_cast: Keira Knightley, Matthew Macfadyen, Brenda Blethyn
blurb: Wright's 2005 adaptation chose atmosphere over wit — rain, light, hands held in restraint. Keira Knightley's Elizabeth became a definitive one for a new generation.

lead_cast: Saoirse Ronan, Emma Watson, Florence Pugh
blurb: Gerwig reordered Alcott's chronology, cutting between the sisters' youth and adulthood. The film reads as a conversation with the novel rather than a transcription of it.

movie_title: The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion the Witch and the Wardrobe
lead_cast: Georgie Henley, Skandar Keynes, William Moseley
book_title: The Lion the Witch and the Wardrobe
blurb: Adamson's adaptation hit Lewis's major beats with Disney gloss. The Christian allegory survived more or less intact, depending on who you asked.

lead_cast: Leonardo DiCaprio, Tobey Maguire, Carey Mulligan
blurb: Luhrmann staged Fitzgerald's novel as spectacle, with modern music under 1920s imagery. The text itself survives, delivered mostly in voice-over.

lead_cast: Gary Oldman, Winona Ryder, Anthony Hopkins
blurb: Coppola added a reincarnated-lover frame that isn't in Stoker. The gothic imagery and Oldman's performance made it the dominant Dracula of its generation.

lead_cast: Tom Hanks, Audrey Tautou, Ian McKellen
blurb: Howard adapted Dan Brown's thriller close to the book. The film arrived with the novel's controversies already attached and did roughly the business you'd expect.

movie_title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
lead_cast: Martin Freeman, Yasiin Bey, Zooey Deschanel
book_title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
blurb: Garth Jennings tried to compress Adams's sprawl into one film. Fans of the radio series and TV serial were divided; newcomers often arrived confused.

lead_cast: Dev Patel, Freida Pinto, Madhur Mittal
blurb: Boyle took Vikas Swarup's novel and relocated its tone from satire to melodrama. The result swept the Oscars and introduced global audiences to Mumbai's chawls.

lead_cast: Tom Hanks, Robin Wright, Gary Sinise
blurb: Zemeckis's film sanded off Groom's acerbic edges, turning the novel's rougher character into something sweeter. The novel's Forrest went to space; the film's did not.

lead_cast: Brad Pitt, Jonah Hill, Philip Seymour Hoffman
book_title: Moneyball: The Art of Winning an Unfair Game
blurb: Lewis's book introduced sabermetrics to a mass audience. The film kept the central argument — statistical analysis against baseball orthodoxy — and gave it a human face in Billy Beane's unglamorous crusade.

lead_cast: Jesse Eisenberg, Andrew Garfield, Armie Hammer
blurb: Sorkin adapted Mezrich's book but took it in his own direction. Facebook's founders have contested most of the film; it won three Oscars anyway.

lead_cast: Leonardo DiCaprio, Tom Hanks, Christopher Walken
blurb: Spielberg's lightest film in years, built from Frank Abagnale's own account of his teenage con career. Later investigations have cast doubt on how much of the memoir actually happened.

lead_cast: James Franco, Kate Mara, Amber Tamblyn
book_title: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
blurb: Boyle built a feature-length film around a single trapped man. Ralston's own account provided the beats; the film's power is in watching James Franco endure them.

lead_cast: Taraji P. Henson, Octavia Spencer, Janelle Monáe
blurb: Shetterly's book recovered the Black women mathematicians NASA had forgotten. The film compressed the timeline for drama but kept the central injustice in focus.

lead_cast: Russell Crowe, Jennifer Connelly, Ed Harris
blurb: Nasar's biography of John Nash was a dense academic portrait. Howard's film kept the schizophrenia storyline and softened almost everything else.

lead_cast: Aamir Khan, R. Madhavan, Sharman Joshi
blurb: Hirani's film takes the IIT setting and the three-friend spine from Bhagat's novel but reinvents nearly everything else. The result is one of the highest-grossing Hindi films ever made.

lead_cast: Shah Rukh Khan, Aishwarya Rai Bachchan, Madhuri Dixit
blurb: Bhansali's maximalist 2002 version arrived after a century of Devdas adaptations. The novel's doomed love survives under all the chandeliers.

lead_cast: Dev Anand, Waheeda Rehman, Leela Chitnis
blurb: Vijay Anand's film kept Narayan's structure but ran its own direction with the ending. Narayan famously disliked it; audiences made it a classic.

lead_cast: Urmila Matondkar, Manoj Bajpayee, Sanjay Suri
blurb: Dwivedi adapted Amrita Pritam's Partition-era novel with care. Urmila Matondkar's lead performance anchors a film about women abducted across the new border.

lead_cast: Prosenjit Chatterjee, Tota Roy Chowdhury, Aishwarya Rai Bachchan
blurb: Rituparno Ghosh brought Tagore's novel of jealousy and widowhood to screen with Aishwarya Rai in the title role. The adaptation is faithful enough to work as a reading guide.

lead_cast: Saif Ali Khan, Vidya Balan, Sanjay Dutt
blurb: Pradeep Sarkar updated Chattopadhyay's 1914 novella to the 1960s, keeping the romantic core and losing most of its social critique.

lead_cast: Sushant Singh Rajput, Rajkummar Rao, Amit Sadh
blurb: Kapoor's film adapts Bhagat's novel with the Gujarat earthquake and the 2002 riots as its backdrop. The friendship at the centre survives both.

lead_cast: Alia Bhatt, Arjun Kapoor, Amrita Singh
book_title: 2 States: The Story of My Marriage
blurb: Varman's adaptation stays close to Bhagat's semi-autobiographical novel of a Punjabi-Tamil romance. The film trades the book's humour for warmer rom-com beats.

lead_cast: Rekha, Farooq Shaikh, Naseeruddin Shah
blurb: Muzaffar Ali's adaptation of Mirza Hadi Ruswa's Urdu novel became a touchstone for the ghazal-film genre. Rekha's performance has defined the role ever since.

lead_cast: Guru Dutt, Meena Kumari, Waheeda Rehman
blurb: Guru Dutt's production kept Bimal Mitra's novel's melancholy intact. Meena Kumari's Chhoti Bahu remains one of Hindi cinema's great performances.
Pamela Rooks adapted Khushwant Singh's novel of a Punjabi village on the brink of Partition. The film kept the novel's refusal to flinch at what came next.

lead_cast: Priyanka Chopra Jonas, Vivaan Shah, Konkona Sen Sharma
blurb: Vishal Bhardwaj expanded Ruskin Bond's novella into a long comedy of serial widowhood. Priyanka Chopra plays all seven marriages.

lead_cast: Shreya Sharma, Pankaj Kapur, Deepak Dobriyal
blurb: Bhardwaj's small adaptation of Ruskin Bond's novella became a quiet favourite. Pankaj Kapur's performance as the shopkeeper carries the moral weight.

lead_cast: Kal Penn, Irrfan Khan, Tabu
blurb: Mira Nair's film tracks a Bengali family across two generations in America, following Lahiri's novel closely. Irrfan Khan and Tabu give it its gravity.
